core_meaning.primary_meaning: Belal corresponds to the Arabic form بلال and is glossed in this record as “Moisture, freshness.” The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Belal corresponds to the Arabic form بلال (ب ل ل). Its core sense is moisture, freshness, refreshment. Bilāl ('moisture, freshness'), borne by Bilāl ibn Rabāḥ (d. 640), the first muezzin of Islam. The source record's gloss 'Shining, Bright' is unsupported.
